Chapter 12: Death and the Meaning of Life.
Death. It’s that horizon none of us can cross, but it shapes everything we do. No matter how much we try to dodge the thought, it’s always waiting in the background—an unspoken certainty.
Think about sitting by the bedside of someone you love, watching as their time runs out. Suddenly, all those things we usually stress over—work, money, reputation—they just don’t matter anymore. What really counts becomes obvious: love, connection, the choices we’ve made... and the ones we didn’t.
In these raw moments, death isn’t just something that happens at the end of life. It’s like a spotlight, shining on what’s important. It reminds us that time isn’t endless, and every possibility comes with a risk.
Sure, facing this reality can be scary. But, it can also bring a sense of clarity. When you truly confront your own mortality, you have to ask yourself: What actually matters? What kind of life do you want to create?
Most of the time, we push these questions away. We bury ourselves in routines, distractions, and the day-to-day rush. But whenever the truth about death sneaks its way in, we get a unique opportunity. We can choose to live more honestly—to make decisions that line up with what really matters, instead of just drifting along.
And here’s the thing: meaning isn’t handed to us. It’s not something we find outside ourselves. Each of us has to create our own meaning, especially in the face of life’s limits.
So, to truly live is to accept that death is real—and let that fact shape the way we move through our days. That’s how every moment becomes more precious, and every choice, a chance to live authentically.
